differences.what: massing: the main block two storeys over a raised basement under its mansard, the Prairie front from its north projection (x 966) to the south-west corner (x 1312) and the 18th Street flank to its east end (x 1491); the cornice's top at y 319-393 and the curb's about 120 px over it
differences.how: T-1880, T-3158: the render's corners at x 966, 1313 and 1491 against the plate's 967, 1312 and 1492, the cornice within 2-7 px

differences.what: the portico across the front's north part on columns, the balustraded balcony over it, and the stoop rising at its north end
differences.how: T-3159: the render's portico and balcony stand within about 10 px of the plate's (under half a metre at about 22 px a metre); the flight at the portico's north end as the plate draws it

differences.what: the rusticated quoined piers dividing the front into pavilions, the corner pier, and the cornice's modillions over the deep frieze
differences.how: T-3158: the piers in the render fall on the plate's within about 10 px

differences.what: the Prairie front's round-arched windows on both storeys under moulded heads
differences.how: T-3157: the render's arched windows line up with the plate's within 10-20 px (under a metre at the front's scale); the plate's heads read heavier, a profile the vignette cannot measure

differences.what: the tall stack rising behind the tree just west of the corner pier (x about 1293, its top at y 213)
differences.how: T-3161: the deck stack at (20, 13.3), top 19.5 m, its cap at x 1290, y 220

differences.what: the flank's great stack on the 18th Street cornice (T-3161, read off Taylor's photograph 1445) renders at x 1326-1354 rising to y 204; the plate shows sky and branches there
differences.how: the plate is of 1890 or earlier (the book's date) and Taylor's photograph of the 1890s, which shows the 1892 work east of the flank, is later: the plate is evidence of the house before the stack, and the 1904 build keeps it (AGENTS.md rule 11, L-pullman-1729-flank-stack-3161)

differences.what: the 18th Street arcade: the plate's open west arch at about x 1408-1454, the build's at x 1383-1426
differences.how: a gap two pictures and two camera fits disagree about (T-3153): about 1.7 m along the flank at the arcade's scale; the Detroit print, from the same corner, puts the arch where the build stands it (T-3160), and Taylor's photograph 1445 puts it further east still (docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/pullman_house_1729_prairie/taylor-1445-camera.md). The block is not moved until the pictures agree

differences.what: the flank west of the arcade: the plate shows one round-arched window over another between the corner pier and the arcade, where the build cuts a pair on each storey
differences.how: T-3161 read it (Taylor's photograph 1445 shows the same single column); not rebuilt in this run

differences.what: the Prairie dormers' moulded, eared hoods (the plate's large dormer at about x 1200 under a broken pediment); the build lays a plain surround round each arch
differences.how: the same gap as the Detroit print's open difference; not rebuilt in this run

differences.what: the iron cresting round the deck, and the low stone wall on piers along the Prairie Avenue line
differences.how: the plate's 1890 vignette shows neither at its scale (the wall line is a low curb and lawn); the Detroit print and Taylor's photograph, both later, show both, and the 1904 build follows them

differences.what: the walls' colour and the mansard's slate
the building east of the flank at the plate's right edge
differences.how: cut by the vignette's edge, and before the 1892 east addition

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
